DNS dispatching algorithms that use state estimation techniques are able to improve the performance of a Web‐server system in terms of throughput, fairness and response time.
DNS scheduling policies with state information can improve the load balancing performance of the cluster, and that this can be achieved without incurring high communication overhead.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and analysis of novel DNS scheduling algorithms that can effectively control the load of the Web‐server clusters, by using the state estimators to reduce the overhead of the DNS dispatching policies.
a DNS scheduling policy for a Web server cluster that is able to estimate the current load of the cluster and dispatch requests to servers accordingly.
the design of new DNS dispatching algorithms that use state information, and with the analysis of their effectiveness in a Web‐server environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed DNS policies with state estimators can improve the performance of the DNS scheduling algorithm, and that the performance improvement is more significant in the case of the DNS policy with state estimators than in the case of other DNS policies without state estimators.
, in a realistic scenario for Web‐server clusters, the DNS dispatching algorithms that incorporate the state estimators proposed in this paper are the most effective ones.
the use of state information in DNS dispatching is a very promising approach for the design of scalable Web‐server architectures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed DNS dispatching policies are effective in reducing the average response time for the Web clients and the average load for the Web servers in a cluster, and that these policies can be implemented with low overhead.
, by using a simple state estimator, a DNS dispatching policy can be improved significantly.
the DNS dispatching policies are effective for controlling the load of Web clusters, provided that the state estimators are used to obtain the system state information.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the DNS dispatcher can be an effective tool for controlling the load of a Web cluster, and the performance of DNS dispatching algorithms can be significantly improved by incorporating state estimation mechanisms.
DNS dispatching policies that incorporate state estimators can be effective for Web‐server clusters, even if the state estimators are based on very simple heuristics.

the DNS can be used as the load balancing mechanism of a Web‐server farm with a very low cost in the form of a small amount of state information that can be easily estimated with low computation overhead and low communication overhead.
